honestCall: The reconciliation pass genuinely fixed every citation iteration-8 flagged: all five edge-tts staleness sites (Goal 1, C1's LATENCY bullet, OQ1, OQ6, §4's RED plan) are now consistently Pipecat/Kokoro-worded; the fabricated dial.js citation is corrected to the verified scheduler.js:81 location; the HMAC auth-carryover requirement is now explicit and matches the live signCtx call order exactly; the build/deploy artifact for the new Python service is named; and OQ8's Kokoro-footprint claim was correctly downgraded from an unvetted '$0/instant' assumption to a benchmark-before-ship requirement. Point-fixing was thorough and accurate. But the process gap iteration-8's own FIND-310 named -- 'a rewrite applied as a local patch without a pass over the document's other sections that reference the same subsystem' -- reproduced itself at three NEW locations this iteration: C1's own INTEGRATION bullet (line 57) still poses the OQ7 Node/Python split as an open (a)/(b) choice with text verbatim-unchanged from the original FIND-307 citation, even though §5's OQ7 entry (line 114) was separately rewritten to RESOLVED with a concrete decision -- the two sections of the same document now directly disagree on whether the single highest-impact architectural decision in the pivot is made. C1's LATENCY bullet claims the Kokoro footprint is 'verified in OQ8' while OQ8 itself says 'OPEN'. And OQ1's new 'JA-confirmed' claim for Smart Turn v3 was added without the citation FIND-305's own fix explicitly required, and is not even repeated in C1's own STACK bullet describing the same component. None of these are re-litigations of the Pipecat decision itself (still judged correct); all three are the document failing to be a single coherent source of truth about decisions it has ALREADY made -- which is precisely what caused the prior FAIL.
